title: Ask on Demand: Targeted Peer Communication for Parallel Agentic Systems
abstract: arXiv:2610.41378v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Parallel LLM agents tackle complex tasks by exploring multiple trajectories, yet useful discoveries remain isolated in individual execution histories. Existing sharing methods often select or summarize information before other agents' needs become clear, potentially overlooking details that become important later. We propose Ask on Demand (AOD), a communication framework that enables agents to seek targeted peer assistance when specific information needs arise. Upon an approved request, AOD retrieves relevant evidence from peer execution histories, selects a suitable peer, and generates a response tailored to the request. To determine when such assistance is worthwhile, we train a lightweight gate using paired team continuations, with supervision derived from final team outcomes and inference cost. translated_title: 按需求助：面向并行智能体系统的定向同伴通信
translated_abstract: 并行LLM智能体通过探索多条轨迹来应对复杂任务，然而有用的发现往往孤立地存在于各个执行历史之中。现有的共享方法通常在其他智能体的需求尚未明确时就进行信息选择或总结，可能忽视后来才变得重要的细节。我们提出了Ask on Demand（AOD），一个使智能体在出现特定信息需求时能够寻求定向同伴协助的通信框架。在请求获得批准后，AOD会从同伴的执行历史中检索相关证据，选择合适的同伴，并生成针对该请求定制的回复。为了判断何时值得寻求此类协助，我们利用成对的团队延续过程训练了一个轻量级门控，其监督信号来自最终团队结果与推理成本。在AppWorld和WebShop上的实验表明，AOD在持续提升任务性能方面优于独立并行执行，同时……
tldr: 该论文提出按需求助（AOD）框架，让并行LLM智能体在出现具体信息需求时向同伴定向求助，通过轻量级门控判断求助时机，从同伴执行历史检索证据并生成定制回复，在AppWorld和WebShop上持续提升任务性能。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes Ask on Demand (AOD), a framework that enables parallel LLM agents to seek targeted peer assistance when specific information needs arise, using a lightweight gate to decide when to ask, consistently improving task performance on AppWorld and WebShop.
